captures.q: What are the arguments in “Locating the Dependencies: A Protocol for Testing Whether Biography, Catalogue and Chronology Are Independent Witnesses” by Lee Sharks? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE PROTOCOL READ AS A PROTOCOL, THE WITHDRAWALS CARRIED, THE SECOND NAME LEFT OUT: asked for the arguments of Locating the Dependencies, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1602 (chip: Goodreads ×5) and keeps its rule: agreement can be 'a property of the derivation', dependence shown 'case by case and only case by case'; columns A, B and C, all three required; the sphere-count case (Metaphysics Λ 8 and On First Principles 5a21–23) located, not established, the evidence running against it; the aconite case reversed by the order in Diogenes (the epigram 996 characters after the report attributed to Eumelus), the earlier claim withdrawn; the lisp (Timotheus), the ages (70, 63), the οἱ δέ doublet; the circularity audit as the outstanding task; 'What stands' in its four statuses; the three overclaiming versions. It cites v3 of 8 September 2026, the archive and AXN:0692. It names Aristotle throughout and never the author of On First Principles; the paper names Theophrastus, and its open question is the catalogue's assignment of the two texts to two names.

atoms.evidence: The central argument of Lee Sharks’s
Locating the Dependencies: A Protocol for Testing Whether Biography, Catalogue and Chronology Are Independent Witnesses
Verdict: the dependency is located, not established.
Sharks identifies a problem in the reconstruction of the Peripatetic corpus

The text makes this argument by correcting two earlier versions of Sharks’s own analysis, setting out a three-part test for dependence, applying it to two cases involving the ancient tradition about Aristotle and the Peripatetics
The rule is strict: a dependency is established only when all three columns are filled.
Sharks observes that three successive versions of the essay overclaimed: each replaced a refuted claim with a structurally similar one and treated the replacement as demonstrated.
